subtitle: Task Manager & Network Port Monitor
empty_none: No ports match your search or filter
empty_pinned: No pinned ports yet — right-click a card and choose Pin Port
core_body:
Ending {name} (PID {pid}) is blocked.

This process is a core part of Windows. Terminating it can trigger a blue screen (BSOD) or crash the whole system, so PortManager will never end it.
self_body: PortManager can't end itself. Use Quit from the tray menu (or Ctrl+Q) to close it.
sys_body:
{name} (PID {pid}) is part of Windows. Ending it can break Windows features, sign you out, or crash the system.

Continue only if you are absolutely sure.
cf_end_note: PID {pid} · port {port}/{proto}. The app is asked to close first.
cf_kill_note: PID {pid} · port {port}/{proto}. It stops immediately — unsaved data is lost.
cf_tree_note: PID {pid} · port {port}/{proto}. The process and every child process stop immediately.
cf_restart_note: PID {pid} · port {port}/{proto}. It is stopped, then started again with its original command line and folder.
clean_body: Everything listening on a dev port is stopped together with its child processes.
msg_startup_fail: Could not update the Windows startup entry.
res_not_closed: did not close — try Force Kill
res_not_ended: did not exit — try Force Kill
set_locales_hint: To add a language, drop a .json file with a "_meta" header into the locales folder, then reopen Settings.
set_hotkey_hint: Press Ctrl+Alt+P anywhere in Windows to show or hide PortManager.
set_deep_hint: Flags look-alike Windows names, listeners running from temp/download folders, backdoor-style ports and hidden processes reachable from your network. A heuristic — expect some false positives.
set_protected_hint: Ending a process on one of these ports always needs a strict confirmation.
reset_body: Language, theme, pins, labels, protected ports and every option return to their defaults. This can't be undone.
msg_import_fail: That file is not a valid PortManager settings file.
msg_hotkey_fail: Ctrl+Alt+P is already used by another app.
pp_body:
You added port {port} to your protected ports. {name} (PID {pid}) is listening there.

Continue only if you are sure.
th_masq: Uses a Windows system name but runs from outside the Windows folder
th_temp: Runs from a temporary, download or other user-writable folder
th_port: Listens on a port commonly used by backdoors and remote-access tools
th_hidden: Process details are hidden and the port is reachable from the network (run as Administrator to inspect it)
